thread:
Maya: Just uploaded a perfetto trace showing a tail latency spike around 16:42 UTC. Client->gateway->runtime spans show repeated kernel flips and a burst of KV cache misses. Trace: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234 (uploaded)
perfetto-bot: Perfetto trace uploaded by Maya: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abcd1234
Jae: I pulled the trace — I can see the gateway fanout then a sequence of runtime spans where kernel selection toggles between `select_v2` (long-seq kernel) and `quant_fwd` (short-seq kernel) for nearby requests. Looks like selection oscillation rather than a single outlier.
Rafael: Do we have an nsys or nvprof capture for that window? Need kernel timelines + SM/L2 metrics to confirm whether it's a compute vs memory pathology.
Maya: I grabbed an nsys around the same time. Command I used:
```
nsys profile --output=nsys_2205001234 --trace=cuda,cudnn --capture-range-end=cpu_activity --force-overwrite
```
Snippets from the nsys summary I exported:
```
kernel select_v2   12.3ms   sm_eff=0.62   l2_hit=0.41
kernel quant_fwd   3.1ms    sm_eff=0.85   l2_hit=0.72
KVCache::Lookup     miss_count=18   window=5s
```
Jae: That lines up — the `select_v2` spikes coincide with a cluster of KVCache misses. Sounds like eviction/thrashing in the KV cache causing sequence length estimation or padding to change, which flips kernel choice.
Ava: Can we reproduce? Suggest running the client->gateway load with Poisson arrivals and a wide seq_len distribution (median~256, 95th~2048) and enable runtime kernel tracing: `--trace-kernels=1`.
Rafael: I'll run an AB: compare `batching.heuristic=auto` vs `batching.heuristic=fixed` and toggle `kvcache.prefetch=2`. Running on the dev-dedicated cluster pinned to 8 GPUs now.
perfetto-bot: nsys capture uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-traces/2205001234/nsys_trace_a.qdrep
Maya: Quick stats from the trace: problematic requests have seq_len distribution where many were between 1024-1200. Hypothesis: the chooser has a threshold at ~1024 and padding or batch composition pushes effective sequence length over that boundary, so it picks the heavier `select_v2` kernel even when most tokens are short.
Jae: Another angle: if KVCache hit ratio is low for the batch, we get more memory traffic and slower kernel, but the chooser ignores cache hit metrics today. We should consider using recent KV hit ratio as a tie-breaker in kernel selection.
Ava: I'll file a perf regression ticket and assign it to runtime-kernel. Action items: reproduce trace + attach nsys + perfetto, add per-token histograms, and test a guard that biases toward short-seq kernel when KV hit ratio > 0.6. ETA for initial triage: EOD tomorrow.
Rafael: AB run started. Will post perfetto link and the per-batch composition when it's done.
Maya: Thanks — @Rafael please also capture `--emit-batch-composition` so we can see request IDs per batch and align with kernel flips. :eyes:
Jae: If AB reproduces, quick temporary mitigation: make chooser prefer `quant_fwd` for batches with >70% short requests, regardless of padded length. That should reduce tail while we fix selection heuristics.
Rafael: Ack. Capturing additional metrics now. Will update with links.
Maya: Great, please paste perfetto + nsys links here when available. I'll start drafting an eval harness to reproduce with synthetic workloads. :thumbsup:
